content.overview: Inventory discrepancies and waste workflows must remain reconstructable from source identity through final disposition. Learners practice preserving evidence, keeping unresolved material separate, reconciling physical and recorded status, and documenting disposition without inventing a universal destruction method or platform workflow.

vocabulary.definition: A difference between expected and observed identity, quantity, status, location or event information that has not yet been resolved.
The authorized decision about what happens to material, such as use, transfer, return, hold, waste, destruction or another locally defined outcome.
A time-ordered record of who or what controlled the material as it moved through the applicable workflow.
The ability to use reliable records to understand the identity, events, locations and final outcome of material over time.

sections.title: A discrepancy remains evidence until it is resolved
sections.body: A mismatch can result from counting, delayed entry, wrong identity, unrecorded movement, duplicate events or another control failure. Technicians gather permitted facts, preserve the current physical and recorded states, and escalate when the difference cannot be reconciled under procedure.

sections.title: Waste still has genealogy
sections.body: Material designated as waste remains connected to its source and event history until the applicable facility and jurisdiction process is complete. GS1 traceability principles reinforce maintaining relationships between traceable objects and lifecycle events; this course applies that technology-neutral logic without prescribing a cannabis destruction method.

sections.title: Physical and digital disposition must agree
sections.body: A record that says material was destroyed when the physical material still exists—or physical disposal that occurred without the required controlled event—creates a traceability failure. The technician preserves the mismatch rather than treating either state as automatically correct.

workedExamples: A waste container lacks a source identifier, so it remains separate until identity is resolved instead of being combined with identified waste.
A system shows destruction complete while the physical material remains; the mismatch is reported and preserved rather than ignored.
Waste created from a split harvest remains linked to the applicable source batch/container relationship and required quantity information.
A physical quantity differs from the pre-disposition record, so the discrepancy is reconciled before the authorized event is finalized.
A technician records the event facts and responsible roles but does not invent witness, approval or destruction requirements that belong to a different jurisdiction or facility.
commonMistakes: Discarding questionable material before identity and status are documented.
Changing records to eliminate an unexplained discrepancy.
Combining unidentified waste with identified waste because all of it is destined for disposal.
Treating 'waste' as the end of traceability rather than another controlled status/event.
Recording disposition complete before the physical event occurred.
Assuming one destruction method, witness rule or seed-to-sale workflow applies in every jurisdiction.
content.practicalApplication: Investigate a mock discrepancy and waste packet containing identified and unidentified material, a quantity mismatch, a premature digital disposition entry and one valid completed event. Reconstruct the source/event history, identify what must remain separate, and produce a vendor-neutral handoff for the authorized disposition process.
content.summary: Traceable waste handling requires preserved source identity, event history, quantity/status evidence and honest physical-versus-record reconciliation. Technicians document what is known and let the authorized local process determine final disposition or destruction.

blocks.title: Waste does not stop being traceable because it will be discarded
blocks.body: A waste or destruction workflow should remain connected to source material and controlled event history until the applicable local process is complete. The stable traceability questions still apply: what material is this, where did it come from, what event placed it into this status, what quantity is involved where required, who controls the next decision, and what ultimately happened?

blocks.title: Waste-lineage questions
rows: Exact source identity and material description
Required physical count/weight/volume before and through disposition where applicable
Quantity changed with no explainable event
Record says disposed while material remains staged
Hold, transfer, waste designation, destruction/disposition event
Final record exists without a matching physical event
Required attribution, approval or witness under the actual local process
Event cannot be tied to responsible roles
Relationship from waste/disposition material back to the applicable plant, batch, lot or container
Waste mixed before source relationships are preserved

blocks.title: Keep a waste or disposition event reconstructable

items.title: Confirm source identity
items.body: Tie the material to the controlled plant, batch, lot, container, room or other source identity required by the facility process.

items.title: Reconcile physical quantity/status
items.body: Capture the required physical measure and compare it with the current controlled record before final disposition.

items.title: Keep unresolved material separate
items.body: Do not combine unidentified or discrepant material with other waste if doing so would erase needed evidence.

items.title: Preserve status before disposition
items.body: Maintain the required hold, waste or other controlled state until the authorized process permits the next event.

items.title: Record the authorized event
items.body: Capture method, time, location, responsible roles, witnesses or other fields actually required by the controlling local workflow.

items.title: Reconcile final physical and record state
items.body: Confirm the controlled record and physical outcome describe the same completed disposition event.

items.title: Preserve the source-to-disposition chain
items.body: Keep enough event history to reconstruct how the original material reached the final state.

left.label: Traceable
left.body: A waste container remains linked to source material, required quantity information, current status, authorized disposition event and final record until the workflow is complete.

right.label: Untraceable
right.body: Questionable material is discarded or mixed into general waste before identity and status are resolved, destroying evidence needed to reconstruct what happened.

blocks.title: A waste container has no source identifier
blocks.setting: A container marked as cultivation waste is staged for the next disposal step, but the source batch or material identity cannot be confirmed. Another identified waste container is beside it.
blocks.prompt: What should the technician do first?
options: Combine the containers because both are waste
Estimate the missing identity from room location
Keep the unidentified material separate, preserve its current state, and escalate the identity problem under procedure before combining or disposing it
Discard the unidentified container immediately so it cannot be confused with good material
blocks.answer: Keep the unidentified material separate, preserve its current state, and escalate the identity problem under procedure before combining or disposing it.
blocks.feedback: Disposal intent does not remove the need for reconstructable identity and status. Combining or discarding the material can erase evidence needed to resolve the discrepancy.

blocks.title: The system says destroyed, but the material is still present
blocks.setting: The tracking record shows a waste container's disposition as complete at 10:15. At 10:30 the identified physical container is still sealed in the staging area and no authorized person can confirm the physical event occurred.
options: Dispose of it immediately so reality matches the record
Ignore it because the system is controlled
Preserve the physical material and record state, document the mismatch, and escalate for authorized reconciliation
Delete the digital event and recreate it later without preserving the change
blocks.answer: Preserve the physical material and record state, document the mismatch, and escalate for authorized reconciliation.
blocks.feedback: The discrepancy is evidence. The technician should not manufacture physical reality to fit the record or silently erase record history.

blocks.title: Vendor-neutral waste / disposition event record
blocks.description: Exact fields are facility- and jurisdiction-specific. These fields illustrate stable traceability questions a controlled disposition event may need to answer.

fields.label: Source identity
fields.value: Plant, batch, lot, container, room or other controlled source

fields.label: Material description
fields.value: What material entered the waste/disposition workflow

fields.label: Pre-event quantity / status
fields.value: Required physical measure and controlled status before disposition where applicable

fields.label: Reason / decision
fields.value: Why the material is held for waste, return, destruction or another disposition

fields.label: Authorized event
fields.value: The local approved disposition/destruction step or decision

fields.label: Time / location
fields.value: When and where the physical event occurred

fields.label: Responsible roles
fields.value: Operator, approver, witness or system attribution actually required locally

fields.label: Final physical state
fields.value: What physically happened to the identified material

fields.label: Reconciliation / exception
fields.value: Any difference between physical and recorded state and how it was routed

blocks.note: Use the actual facility and jurisdiction process for required methods, approvals, witnesses, system entries and legal requirements.

blocks.title: Audit a discrepancy and waste lineage packet
blocks.instructions: Review a mock record set containing one unresolved inventory mismatch, one valid waste event, one unidentified waste container and one premature disposition entry.
prompts: Reconstruct the source identity and event chain for each material group.
Separate confirmed facts from possible causes.
Identify which material must remain separate until identity or quantity is resolved.
Identify which actions the Technician I worker may document versus which disposition decisions require another role.
Produce a reconstructable handoff without inventing a jurisdiction-specific destruction rule.
blocks.artifact: Discrepancy, waste-lineage and disposition handoff packet

blocks.title: Remediation cue
blocks.body: If your proposed fix destroys, combines or relabels the material before the discrepancy is reconstructed, you may be deleting the evidence needed to resolve it. Preserve identity, physical state and event history first.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: A material discrepancy is not solved by throwing material away or editing the record. Preserve source identity and event history, reconcile physical and recorded state, and let the authorized local process determine disposition or destruction.
